messages:
maria: seeing a lot of inference pods Pending in gpu-pool-1 starting ~10:07, cluster-autoscaler didn't react
aj: can you paste `kubectl describe pod` for one pending?
maria: sure, here's the last part: 
```
Events:
  Type     Reason            Age   From               Message
  ----     ------            ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2m    default-scheduler  0/5 nodes are available: 5 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
```

aj: CA should bring up nodes if pods request `nvidia.com/gpu`. Are pods requesting GPU?
maria: yes, spec has `resources.requests: {"nvidia.com/gpu": 1}`. But CA log shows: 
```
I0323 10:09:31 cluster_autoscaler.go:XXX] Not scaling: failed to find nodegroup for labels: node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: gpu-a2
```
tom: that log smells like nodegroup/labels mismatch between ASG/node pool names and CA config. Also saw quota errors earlier in the region.
lee: fwiw we've had region QuotaLimit reached for GPU on that AZ — that prevents nodepool from provisioning even if CA asks. CA should surface that in events though.
maria: interesting — autoscaler-bot posted a scale event then immediately a failure: 
autoscaler-bot: cluster-autoscaler: scale-up: triggered by pod/infra-inference-xyz, nodegroup=gpu-pool-1 desired=3->4 reason: unschedulable pods
autoscaler-bot: cluster-autoscaler: scale-up failed: InstanceQuotaExceeded: Requested GPUs exceed quota in europe-west2

aj: so two converging problems: (1) CA was asked but quota prevented nodes, (2) HPA maybe spiking because of custom metric causing surge. Any HPA config?
maria: HPA.yaml excerpt: 
```
metrics:
  - type: External
    external:
      metric:
        name: queue_depth_per_replica
      target:
        type: AverageValue
        averageValue: "50"
```

lee: that `AverageValue` with a low sample window plus noisy queue depth will cause rapid up/down. VPA is also enabled in the namespace and recommended lower CPU which reduces pod resource requests -> fewer pods fit per node -> more pods -> loop.
nate: i've seen that exact cascade: VPA down-recs lower CPU, HPA reacts to more pods for the same throughput, CA tries to scale GPU nodes, quota fails, backpressure, request latency skyrockets.
aj: couple quick mitigations: (a) add metric smoothing (use Prometheus adapter with `rate()` or movingAvg), (b) set HPA stabilizationWindowSeconds and scaling policies to avoid instant bursts, (c) pin VPA to only recommend and not automatically evict, or set lower minAllowed resources.
maria: adding stabilizationWindow sounds good. any config snippets?
aj: example: 
```
behavior:
  scaleUp:
    stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300
    policies:
      - type: Percent
        value: 50
        periodSeconds: 60
  scaleDown:
    stabilizationWindowSeconds: 600
```

lee: also change external metric to `targetAverageValue: "75"` and use a 30s PromQL smoothing: `avg_over_time(queue_depth[30s])` in the adapter. That will reduce spike sensitivity.
tom: on CA side: mark nodepool with correct labels that match CA nodegroup config, or update CA's node-group discovery. Also we can configure CA to fall back to a cheaper non-GPU nodepool for spillover (if model supports CPU fallback) by using node affinity and tolerations + a lower-tier variant of the model.
ate: cost note: if we spill to CPU fallback it will reduce latency but increase inference cost per request sometimes — need product ok.
maria: ops immediate plan: 1) update HPA behavior to include stabilizationWindow/scale policy 2) change Prometheus adapter query to avg_over_time 3) flip VPA to recommendation-only for this ns 4) open quota ticket with cloud team to increase GPU quota in europe-west2 or move to another region 5) add CA alert when scale-up fails due to quota.
aj: + add pod annotation to require `nvidia.com/gpu` explicitly so we avoid mismatch with different GPU resource names. Also check nodeSelector and taints: if gpu nodes are tainted `gpu=true:NoSchedule` pods need tolerations.
maria: confirmed pods have tolerations and nodeSelector, so likely a label mismatch in CA discovery + quota. i'll do the HPA/VPA changes first to stabilize traffic.
autoscaler-bot: cluster-autoscaler: next check in 2m — currently 4 unschedulable pods, scale-up not attempted due to quota.
lee: we should also add a circuit breaker in the inference service to shed load (reject new requests) if queue depth > 500 for > 1m — fast fix to stop runaway cost/latency.
tom: agree. Also add a canary: deploy a small `gpu-reserve` nodepool with min 1 to avoid cold-start on spikes for critical customers. cost tradeoff but improves SLO.
maria: i'll open a PR with the HPA behavior and prometheus adapter change, and a ticket for quota + gpu-pool label sync. tagging @aj @lee for review.
aj: thanks — i'll look at CA discovery config after lunch.
nate: ping me for VPA tweaks — i'll lock it to recommendation-only for now.
maria: thanks all :thumbsup:
